about: Photo textures (task 007): what tools/textures.mjs makes, and from what. A ground texture is the 2025 orthophoto over a tile. A facade is a reference photo (refs/photos.json, by its id) straightened onto a wall: wall is the wall's points on the map, left to right as the photo sees it (along a building's footprint); quad its corners in the photo's own pixels, top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left; s the metres along the wall they span (from its first point, the whole wall if left out); y the metres above the building's ground (its y) at the quad's bottom and top. Read off the photo by eye.

textures.notes: Fujacal, the shooter's area: seven of the viewpoints.
The middle of three. Its front steps back twice; the top metre of the taller part is left out. Dusk, a parked car at its foot.
Two blocks under one outline: the right one a floor taller, its top floor left out.
Taken from a moving car: blurred. Only the shops and the first floor; the top floor is out of the photo.
Most of the retail park's front: the ends are out of the photo, and a dark blur on the right is the car's window frame.
The café's ground floor, which the LiDAR found as a building of its own; a car hides its left end.
The corner block from its corner; its left end is out of the photo. A lamp post and cars in front.
The left of a pair of semi-detached houses, its azulejos. The garden wall and fence stand in front of its lowest floor.
A narrow part of a long block, where the map cuts it; a lorry hides the ground floor.
The middle of three blocks, its top floor set back and left out; the map's outline is wider than the block, so a little of each neighbour comes too.
Seen from across a car park, so 5 cm a pixel at best.
